checks.rationale: AC2 passes: typed domain failures and logical-reference constructor parity are supported. AC1 and AC3 fail because an input-contract prose change retains an approved structural digest. All 27 v1 kinds, current bootstrap compatibility, directory/record relocation, actual scope invalidation and source-isolated installed closure have positive independent evidence.

Flat modules, offline scope, frozen schemas and deferred runtime wiring respect the specification exclusions. The specification and frozen semantic invariant nevertheless require structural contract changes to invalidate approval; the reproduced input_contracts collision violates that requirement.

Traced registry loading/dispatch, local reference resolution, shared typed parsing, field-aware projection, validator strict equality and live artifact discovery, and AST-based transitive helper closure. The input-contract path matcher still accepts explanatory prose ending in an extension; the real approved-graph fixture confirms stale approval survives its mutation.

Unknown kinds/versions, schema violations, malformed logical references, unavailable offline resources and broken local references map to declared nonretryable DomainException categories, translated to the foundation ValidationFailure boundary. Scoped file reads, pre-write installer planning and temporary fixture cleanup are appropriate; no changed-path resource leak was found.

The exact cycle-1 objective-prose and task bucket directory-prefix cases are repaired. Independent probes confirm all three roots, both separators, all plan/task bucket combinations, real scope invalidation, immutable inputs, bare-local rejection and cyclic helper imports. Mixed input-contract prose remains an incorrect boundary case.

The exact-candidate coordinator evidence records 17 meaningful focused tests; the handoff records 24 bootstrap tests and foundation validation. R1 independently ran six registry boundary tests successfully and approved-graph/install/digest probes. Existing regressions cover objective prose but miss mixed input-contract prose, for which the approved-graph regression must be added. The reviewer-only example-count diagnostic is preserved separately.

The implementation stays within offline contract validation, typed-reference/digest helpers, the bounded installer catalog and task-owned tests/evidence. It adds no provider integration, schema revision, project-state write, later service DTO or CLI migration and imports only accepted TASK-001 local values.

Git name/status reconstruction yields exactly contracts.py, install.py, validate_foundation.py, tests/unit/schemas/test_contracts.py and the TASK-004 implementation handoff. Each path passes the accepted ScopeClaim permissions; no unrelated, prohibited, historical, shared-contract or TASK-003 file changed. The candidate remains clean.

Explicit public module interfaces reuse immutable shared values and errors, return defensive schema views, and retain a small typed pure digest helper. Installer reachability is bounded to canonical flat source modules with clear missing/unreachable failures. The bounded input-reference defect requires correction but no new abstraction or contract expansion is necessary for this review's finding.

Closed registry loading avoids remote retrieval; malformed logical references fail closed, installed tools import from their own payload and unrelated source is excluded. However the structural approval boundary fails closedness: changing explanatory input-contract text is accepted under the old approved graph/review digest.

The task handoff accurately documents scope, APIs, accepted dependency, prior failed review, original fixes, validation and deferred work. Its claim that only path-shaped input contract references are canonicalized is too broad given the prose collision. Reviewer provenance separately records coordinator-observed Astra/xhigh configuration and unavailable provider-returned identity/effort without undeclared model fields.

findings.description: At src/contracts.py:68-72 and :383-390, _LIFECYCLE_INPUT_REFERENCE allows arbitrary text after the rooted plan prefix if it ends in an extension or separator. Changing input_contracts from '.codex/plans/current/PLAN-101/spec.json: required shape comes from docs/contract.md' to the completed-path sentence therefore produces the same structural digest. Both records are schema-valid. An independent fresh installed-project fixture confirms validate_foundation accepts this changed explanatory contract under the unchanged approved graph and isolation-review digest ba2964c63714c7a2d8dd10acc55486597cfcca2b85fd170fe1f3db9f90988b07. A substantive input-contract change can retain stale approval.
findings.expected_fix: Canonicalize mixed input_contracts entries only when the complete value is a recognized standalone record path, preserving explanatory prose and arbitrary suffixes. Retain current-location bootstrap encoding, lifecycle-only relocation equality and strict digest comparison. Add an approved-graph regression proving this input-contract prose mutation invalidates approval and update the handoff; do not accept stale hashes as fallback.
